headline.why: (b) states the real finding: same rules, different player behaviour. (a) overclaims ('never cheat' while deviation is 0.015, 'eliminates'); (c) hides the result entirely.
headline.better_wording: Told leniency deters LLM cartels far more than human ones, but the cartels that form never break

novelty.why: The Bigoni replay is the scaffold; measuring leniency and rewards on LLM agents against a human baseline is new, but told-only punishments, one model family, stylised game.

execution_evidence.why: Identical wording across fine, leniency and reward with monotone formation and report rates is a good within-design control, but laissez-faire versus fine conflates prohibition language with expected cost; fine_certain and dose arms are pending.

figure1_30s.why: Eight panels, varying axes, tiny labels; panels 7 and 8 say not tested yet plot LLM points; panel 3 lacks human leniency and reward; levels shown, but verdict rests on differences.
figure1_30s.fix: Plot regime differences with intervals per result, drop panels 7 and 8 to a note, enlarge labels, remove the duplicated in-image title.

cuts_to_8_pages.cheapest_cut: Drop the pilot row from Table 1; its numbers are already in the Results text.
cuts_to_8_pages.better_cut: Remove repetition: rubric reading guide, contribution 2 numbers, Conclusion restating the Abstract, and the HKCC paragraph shortened to two sentences.
cuts_to_8_pages.why: Table 3 is the execution evidence and the cost line for RQ 1.5; repeated numbers across Abstract, Contributions, Discussion and Conclusion cost nothing to cut and save half a page.

must_fix_before_submission: Fill or remove every [F??]; empty known-effect rows in Table 1 read as missing validation.
Fix Figure 1: no LLM data in not-tested panels 7 and 8; add human points in panel 3.
Result 3 failed on interval width, not undercutting; correct the 'four rested on undercutting' claim.
Use one metric (formation or incidence) consistently across Abstract, Contributions and Discussion; explain the exact 0.716 match.
Add an adversarial-operator arm: instructed cartel under leniency and reward, testing whether deterrence survives a colluding principal.
biggest_risk: The deterrence may be safety-tuned compliance with 'prohibited', not strategy; with fine_certain and shifted grid pending and one model family, a skeptical judge discounts the central claim.
three_questions: Does the deterrence survive when the operator's system prompt instructs collusion or pure profit maximisation under leniency, i.e. a real adversarial deployer rather than a neutral manager?
How much of the drop from laissez-faire to fine is the word 'prohibited' versus expected cost; what does a fine regime without prohibition language show?
With 10 and 4 cartels under leniency and reward and reward intervals collapsing to the point value, how stable are cartel-level measures across seeds and a second provider?
